name: meeple-pool-deep-v1
description: ⛔ 09/09/2026: NO SUBJECT UNDER THE SHIPPED GAME. There are no meeples in the commons (C6), the island seeds none and meeplesPerTile() returns 0, so every island.meeples knob moves nothing unless a meeple control is on - and this overlay does not pin one, so run alone it is a no-op. It is kept because island.json's own unresolved list names it and because the question it asks is still open inside the meeple game; to ask it, add the pins from overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json. THE MEEPLE POOL COMPOSITION ARM (v31, 02/09/2026). The shipped bag is 5 of each of the 5 colours, 25 in total, and that number was chosen for a component reason rather than a design one: 25 is the smallest flat pool that covers the 24 delivery spaces of a 4-seat board. The consequence nobody chose is that the island's colour mix is NEARLY DETERMINISTIC at 4 seats and genuinely random at 2. 24 of 25 meeples are drawn at four players, so the board almost always offers close to five of every action; 12 of 25 are drawn at two players, so it offers a real sample and a two-player island can plausibly show four Draw meeples and no Harvest. The variance in what the island offers is therefore HIGHEST at the seat count with the fewest players competing for it, which is backwards. This arm deepens the bag to 10 per colour, 50 in total, without changing what any single delivery space is worth: at every seat count the island now deals a genuine sample, and 4p stops being a near-perfect five-of-each. Nothing else moves - same 25-to-50 colours, same one meeple per space, same face-up setup. WHAT TO READ, in order: (1) the meeple ECONOMY assertion, earned against spent, which should not move at all - if it does, the arm has changed how attractive deliveries are and the comparison is contaminated; (2) the spread of meeple colours claimed per seat, which is the thing being varied; (3) the suit win rates at 4 seats specifically, because that is the seat count the arm changes most; (4) actions resolved per turn, which must stay flat - the same 24 meeples reach the board either way, so a move here means something else drifted. IF NOTHING MOVES, that is the useful result and the shipped 25 stays: it is the cheaper component and the simpler setup. THE COMPONENT COST IS REAL, so do not adopt this on a delta inside the noise floor - it is 25 more wooden pieces in a small-box game with a five-punchboard budget. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved. ⛔ DELIVERY MEEPLE PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the delivery meeple ON as the shipped default (rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace 1, meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1, meepleSpendDistinctColours false) together with two new island rules, the space choice (rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice true: a delivery names either free space) and the closing draw (rules.turn.closingDrawPerCrate 1: filling a tile draws one card per crate). This overlay predates it, so all six leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-ruling values (deliveryMeepleSpace null, meepleSpendTiming 'start', meepleSpendPerTurn null, meepleSpendDistinctColours false, deliverySpaceChoice false, closingDrawPerCrate 0; 'start' and null are the old inert values, not 'none' and 0) and it still replays its own game.
